WESTMEATH COUNTY COUNCIL Local Authority Development - File Ref. LAA(11)-2025 
Nature and Extent of Development: 
The proposed development is located at the former Belvedere Orphanage Institution, 
Tyrrellspass, County Westmeath. The proposal comprises the construction of five social 
housing units, including the refurbishment of the former Matron’s House to accommodate 
two of the units, together with all associated site development works. 
The works include: 
•
Partial demolition of the existing Matron’s House including legacy rear extensions.
•
Repair and protection of the existing front entrance porch
•
Provision of new, part-single storey, part-two storey extension to the rear of the
existing Matrons House.
•
Alterations to the internal house layout to create 2 no. 2 bedroom dwelling units.
•
Repairs to the front elevation
•
Construction of 3 no. single storey universally accessible dwelling units (1 no.1 bed
& 2 no.2 bed) arranged in courtyard configuration to the rear of the site.
•
Widening to the existing vehicular entrance including provision of 5 communal car
park spaces.
•
Works to the existing site boundary conditions
•
Connections to the public infrastructure and all other associated development, site
works and landscaping.
Location of Proposed Development: Belvedere Orphanage, Tyrrellspass, Co. Westmeath

Project Background 
Westmeath County Council’s Housing Capital Projects Team has submitted a Part 8 planning 
proposal to carry out a development at the site of the former Belvedere Orphanage located 
at Tyrrellspass, County Westmeath. 
The project involves the construction of ﬁve social housing units, including the refurbishment 
of the former Matron’s House to accommodate two of the units, together with all associated 
site development works. 
The project schedule includes the following proposed works: 
•
Partial demolition of the existing Matron’s House including legacy rear extensions.
•
Repair and protection of the existing front entrance porch
•
Provision of new, part-single storey, part-two storey extension to the rear of the
existing Matrons House.
•
Alterations to the internal house layout to create 2 no. 2 bedroom dwelling units.
•
Repairs to the front elevation
•
Construction of 3 no. single storey universally accessible dwelling units (1 no.1 bed
& 2 no.2 bed) arranged in courtyard conﬁguration to the rear of the site.
•
Widening to the existing vehicular entrance including provision of 5 communal car
park spaces.
•
Works to the existing site boundary conditions
•
Connections to the public infrastructure and all other associated development, site
works and landscaping.
The proposed works are located within the Architectural Conservation Area (Tyrrellspass 
Town ACA) and the former Belvedere Matron’s House is a property identified on the NIAH 
15322031 as being of regional importance.

1.0 Site Overview  
The proposed development is situated on the site of the former Belvedere Orphanage, 
located just off the Mullingar Road, to the north of Tyrrellspass village. The site extends to  
 
approximately 0.145 hectares, and comprises a combination of amenity grassland, mature 
trees, hard-surfaced pathways, scrubland, the former Matron’s House & associated 
outbuildings. 
 
The lands are in the ownership of Westmeath County Council. The wider Belvedere 
Orphanage complex, constructed in 1842, is a small-scale institutional grouping comprising 
six detached single and two-storey buildings arranged around a crescent to the south, with 
original gates and boundary wall located to the east. The site is located within the Tyrrellspass 
Architectural Conservation Area (ACA), which is recognised for its architectural character and 
historical significance. 
Figure 1: Site Location Map 
The former Matron’s House is not listed on the Record of Protected Structures; however, it is 
recorded on the NIAH as being of regional importance, thus reinforcing the buildings historic 
importance to the built heritage of the local area and within Westmeath. The categories of 
specialist interest include Architectural, Artistic, Historical and Social. The group of structures

Page 4 of 37 
 
     PART 8 LAA 11-2025 WESTMEATH COUNTY COUNCIL – BELVEDERE ORPHANAGE, TYRRELLSPASS 
known as the Belvedere Orphanage Institution are sited within the Architectural Conservation 
area ‘Belvedere Orphanage’ therefore the setting and exterior appearance of the structures 
are of special interest. Although the buildings are dispersed, they are a unified entity on a 
planned crescent shape mirroring the planned village of Tyrrellspass to the south.  
 
 
Belvedere Orphanage former Matron’s House is included in the NIAH (2004) and is described 
as follows:  
Detached three-bay two-storey former orphanage matron's house on L-shaped plan, built 
c.1840, with projecting single bay gable-fronted entrance porch to centre of front facade 
(southeast). Now in the ownership of Westmeath County Council and currently out of use. 
Pitched natural slate roof with roughcast rendered chimneystack and terracotta pots. Ornate 
timber bargeboards to gable-fronted section to east end and to projecting porch. Roughcast 
rendered walls over smooth rendered plinth course. Recessed smooth rendered horizontal 
panels/fascia to southeast and northwest facades at first floor level.  Square-headed window 
openings with cut stone sills and metal lattice windows with timber mullions.  Oculus window 
with leaded glass above porch to second floor. Square-headed doorcase to porch with plain 
cut stone surround, a battened timber door with square-headed over light above with lattice 
glazing. Set back from road in own grounds with gates and boundary wall to east (15322032).  
Four detached single and two-storey alms houses/orphanage buildings of various styles and 
in various states of repair, arranged around a crescent, to the south. Now boarded up and no 
longer in use.

1.5 Site History 
Planning Files: 
PL 00-1618 
Planning permission sought for the retention and restoration of 5 former 
orphanage buildings, belvedere orphanage, for use as 10 dwellings. Application withdrawn. 
PL 98/1345 – Permission was granted for 12 houses and the retention of the facades and 
creation of new entrance at Mullingar Road.  An Taisce appealed the Council’s decision.  An 
Bord Pleanála refused permission on the following grounds: 
Having regard to the importance of the Tyrrellspass as an historical and tourist center in the 
county, as stated in the current Development Plan for the area, it is considered that the 
proposed development (which includes the partial demolition and inadequate refurbishment 
of the existing buildings of the former Belvedere Orphans Institution) would result in the loss 
of buildings of architectural and historical and heritage value, would fail to respect the 
architectural and historical integrity of the original layout and would be out of character with 
the established pattern of development in the area.  The proposed development would, 
therefore, seriously injure the amenities of the area and would be contrary to the proper 
planning and development of the area.   
Previous Part 8 Schemes: 
 
Part 8: File Ref. LA136 2011:  The retention and restoration and refurbishment of 5 No. 
former (4 standing 1 no. demolished), formerly known as Belvedere orphan Institute or 
Belvedere orphanage, for use as 10 No. dwellings and the construction of a new access road 
and ancillary services. Approval granted.

1.6 Policy Context  
1.6.1 National & Regional Policy Context 
Project Ireland 2040 - Revised National Planning Framework – April 2025 (NPF) 
The National Planning Framework (NPF) sets out a high-level, long-term strategic plan for 
shaping the future growth and sustainable development of Ireland to the year 2040. It is 
underpinned by ten National Strategic Outcomes (NSOs), which reflect the overarching vision 
for balanced regional development, environmental sustainability, economic competitiveness, 
and quality of life. These are supported by a series of more detailed National Policy Objectives 
(NPOs), which guide decision-making at national, regional, and local levels. 
In the context of the proposed project, the following NSOs and NPOs are particularly relevant: 
National Strategic Outcomes (NSOs) 
 
Enhanced Amenities and Heritage 
This outcome supports the protection, preservation, and integration of heritage assets within 
evolving communities which is highly applicable to the retention and adaptive re-use of 
architectural and heritage assets like the Matron’s House within this project.

Compact Growth & Strengthened Rural Economies and Communities 
Revitalising historic urban cores supports compact, heritage-led regeneration a priority that 
fosters sustainable, regionally balanced growth. 
 
National Policy Objectives (NPOs) 
NPO 9 – Compact Growth 
The proposal seeks to deliver new homes within the existing built-up footprint of Tyrrellspass 
to ensure compact growth. 
NPO 67 — Built Heritage & Adaptive Reuse 
This objective aims to promote sustainable reuse and refurbishment of existing buildings and 
structures. This policy directly endorses the subject application’s focus on retaining and 
repurposing the historic building located on site. 
NPO 89 – Heritage Protection and Reuse: 
The proposal demonstrates a commitment to protecting and enhancing cultural and built 
heritage by protecting and preserving the identified property listed on the NIAH, while 
removing non-original additions to enable sensitive future development and adaptive reuse. 
NPO 90 – Heritage Protection: 
The proposal demonstrates enhancement and protection of this built heritage asset within 
the Architectural Conservation Area and streetscape of Tyrrellspass by the appropriate and 
sensitive investment and conservation. 
 
Regeneration & Infrastructure Delivery 
The NPF revision strongly emphasizes compact growth, brownfield development, and 
revitalization of urban cores, including vacant or derelict properties. Reusing vacant 
structures in Tyrrellspass ACA is in keeping with this policy direction. 
The NPF aligns with Town Centre First and Urban and Rural Regeneration approaches, 
promoting the revitalization of historic buildings. 
 
Regional Spatial and Economic Strategy for the Eastern and Midland Region (2019-2031) 
The Regional Spatial and Economic Strategy (RSES) for the Eastern and Midland Region 
provides a long-term, statutory framework to implement Project Ireland 2040, integrating the 
NPF and the NDP. It focuses on coordinated spatial planning, economic development, climate 
action, and aligned infrastructure investment across the region.

The RSES outlines a strategic vision and investment framework to guide future regional 
growth, manage spatial and economic development, and deliver targeted policy responses 
through Regional Policy Objectives (RPOs). This strategy is underpinned by 16 Regional 
Strategic Outcomes (RSOs), which align with national and EU policy and support the delivery 
of the National Strategic Outcomes (NSOs) set out in the NPF. 
The proposed development is consistent with the principles of the RSES, and in particular with  
• RSO 2 – Compact Growth and Urban Regeneration: It facilitates the regeneration of a 
brownfield site within the existing built-up area of Tyrrellspass settlement. The 
development promotes compact urban growth and contributes to the conservation of 
built heritage through the adaptive re-use of a vacant historic property listed on the 
NIAH and located within the Tyrrellspass ACA. 
Future development in Tyrrellspass is expected to focus on compact growth, the regeneration 
of underused or derelict town centre sites, and enhancement of the public realm.  
• RPO 4.8 Support the regeneration of underused town centre and brownfield / infill 
lands along with the delivery of existing zoned and serviced lands to facilitate 
significant population growth and achieve sustainable compact growth targets of 
30% of all new homes to be built within the existing built-up urban area. 
 
Heritage Led Regeneration 
Bringing unused or underused spaces within our towns back into use has many advantages. 
In addition to reviving the economic value of an urban area, it also removes abandoned and 
derelict sites, and reduces the pressure to build on greenfield sites and valuable agricultural 
land. 
Local distinctiveness is key to each town having a unique selling point. The character and 
distinctiveness of the historic built environment are central to the future success of Irish 
towns.  
• RPO 9.27: EMRA will support local authorities to work with local communities to 
promote historic towns in the Region in the practice of heritage led regeneration, to 
promote the sensitive and adaptive reuse of historic building stock and industrial 
structures where appropriate, and to strengthen their capability to draw down 
European and national funding. 
 
Delivering Homes, Building Communities 2025-2030 An Action Plan on Housing Supply and 
Targeting Homelessness. (2025) 
The Delivering Homes, Building Communities provides a long-term, statutory framework to 
implement Project Ireland 2040, integrating the NPF and the NDP. It focuses on providing new

Partial demolition of the existing Matron’s House including legacy rear extensions.

The proposed development will facilitate the re-use and revitalisation of a vacant historic 
building and the compact development of new housing located within the Tyrrellspass ACA. 
The former orphanage matrons house has been vacant for several years prior to it being 
inhabited for 60 years by the same occupant. It is a detached three-bay two-storey structure 
on an L-shaped plan-built c.1840 with projecting single-bay gable fronted entrance porch. It 
is in a poor state of repair, however much of its historic fabric both externally and internally 
survives. 
The proposed development includes the provision of 3 no. new single storey dwellings to the 
rear of the Matrons House. It is noted that the provision of the new development is justified 
on the basis that it will give rise to the restoration of the Matrons House. The submitted AHIA 
states the impact of the proposal as moderate. It further states ‘The proposed layout respects 
the historic building lines and preserves the open space character that defines the 'urban' feel 
of the Belvedere Orphanage scheme. The new dwellings are arranged in a courtyard style 
mimicking the planned village feel.’ The AHIA states that ‘the new units are designed to 
respect the Crescent’s unique geometry, upholding the original architectural vision of the 
Countess,’ 
The Architectural Conservation Officer has reviewed the development proposals and 
considers that the proposed new development of 3 no. new single storey dwellings will impact 
on the immediate curtilage of the structure and the Architectural Conservation Area. 
However, the impact is somewhat mitigated by its siting within the back land area to the rear 
of the Matrons House. The proposed development will adapt and bring back into use the 
former Matrons House, thus ensuring the long-term conservation of the structure, which is in 
accordance with best conservation practice. 
The new development of 3 units will be screened and the visual impact of the development 
reduced when viewed from the main road, due to the topography of the site and the planned 
retention of existing mature trees to the front of the site.

1.8 Architectural Heritage  
The town of Tyrrellspass has an attractive and distinctive built form and has been designated 
as an Architectural Conservation Area (ACA) to protect its character. It is the policy of 
Westmeath County Development Plan 2021 to: 
CPO 14.39, to ‘Promote development that positively contributes to the character and 
appearance of the Architectural Conservation Area. New development or alterations to 
existing building(s) in an ACA shall respect the special character of the ACA and reflect the 
historic architecture in terms of scale, design and materials used. Regard shall be had to any 
guidance contained in the Statement of Characters prepared for ACAs.’ 
CPO 14.40 to ‘Consider development proposals within ACAs in accordance with the Statements 
of Character prepared for ACAs in Castlepollard, Kilbeggan, Moate, Tyrrellspass, Mullingar 
and Athlone’. 
An Architectural Heritage Impact Assessment (AHIA) was submitted as part of the Part VIII 
documentation. The AHIA outlines that the character and special features of the Matron’s 
House will in the main be protected through the proposed works with some of the works 
causing moderate impacts. The AHIA, concludes that the use of the building as residential is

Page 18 of 37 
 
     PART 8 LAA 11-2025 WESTMEATH COUNTY COUNCIL – BELVEDERE ORPHANAGE, TYRRELLSPASS 
compatible with the zoning of the site. Conservation works to the existing dwelling shall be 
carried out in accordance with best practice to protect the long-term use of the dwelling. 
The current application represents the formal realization of the conservation strategy 
established during the 2001 works, which identified the Matron’s House for future 
restoration. The proposed intervention is a critical mitigation measure against the ongoing 
loss of historic fabric. By undertaking essential stabilisation now, the project fulfils a primary 
conservation objective: preventing "demolition by neglect" and securing the building’s long-
term survival.  
The AHIA identifies a number of specific grounds supporting the proposed residential 
conversion of the property. The conversion of the Matron’s House into two units is justified 
having regard to the following heritage principles: 
• Historical Continuity: The proposal respects a 180-year evolution of the site, 
mirroring its long-standing transition from institutional to domestic use. 
• Fabric Preservation & Reversibility: The design prioritizes the protection of surviving 
19th-century elements including lattice windows, original shutters, and staircases, 
thus ensuring that modern interventions remain sympathetic and reversible. 
• ACA & Geometrical Integrity: As a cornerstone of this "small-scale complex," the 
development adheres strictly to the established plan form. The new units are 
 
designed to respect the Crescent’s unique geometry, upholding the original architectural 
vision of the Countess. The report states that the works will not have a negative impact on 
the special interest of the Matron’s House and the immediate ACA and will allow sustainable 
on-going use of the building. 
The WCC Conservation Architect has reviewed the plan proposals and advises as follows: 
The development of the former Matrons House and its subdivision into 2 no separate units is 
positive and welcome in bringing the structure back into use. The existing rear extensions are 
poorly constructed later additions to the original plan of the Matron’s House.  It is considered 
their demolition and replacement with a new rear extension is deemed appropriate. Subject 
to minor design modifications the works to the Matrons House is acceptable.  
Regarding the proposed development to the rear of the matron’s house. The historic plan 
layout of the structures associated with the orphanage are arranged around a crescent 
mirroring the village crescent of Tyrellspass to the south. The construction of the new 
development of 3 no. single storey dwellings will interrupt the historic design intention. 
However, the siting of the development to the rear of the Matron’s house will mitigate the

Parking Arrangements

used for the carparking spaces. 
 
1.9 Water and Waste Water Services Provision 
 
Water and foul water connections are required in association with the proposed works.  
Uisce Éireann were consulted as part of the process and they have confirmed that a Pre-
Connection Enquiry (PCE) was submitted and that a Confirmation of Feasibility (COF) was 
issued to the applicant.

Water Supply - The COF confirms that in relation to water supply a connection is feasible 
without infrastructure upgrade. 
Wastewater - The COF confirms that a connection is feasible subject to upgrades.  The 
nearest UÉ foul sewer is approximately 30 metres from the site boundary. UÉ have no plans 
to extend this foul sewer towards the proposed site. The applicant would be fully liable for 
the cost of works associated with extending this foul sewer for the purpose of gaining a 
connection.   
 
UÉ notes a history of basement flooding in the downstream properties also owned by the

prior to connection application.  
The applicant shall enter into a Connection Agreement(s) with Uisce Éireann to provide for a 
service connection(s) to the public water supply and/or wastewater collection network and 
adhere to the standards and conditions set out in that agreement.

Architectural Conservation Officer 
Report received 16 July 2026. The report confirms that the former orphanage Matrons House 
is recorded on the National Inventory of Architectural Heritage, Ref No. 15322031 as being of 
regional importance but is not listed on the RPS. The listing on the NIAH highlights its 
importance to the built heritage of the local area and to Westmeath. The categories of 
specialist interest include Architectural, Artistic, Historical and Social. The group of structures 
known as the Belvedere Orphanage Institution are sited within the Architectural Conservation 
area ‘Belvedere Orphanage’ therefore the setting and exterior appearance of the structures 
are of special interest. Although the buildings are dispersed, they are a unified entity on a 
planned crescent shape mirroring the planned village of Tyrrellspass to the south.  
The former orphanage matrons house has been vacant for several years prior to it being 
inhabited for 60 years by the same occupant. It is a detached three-bay two-storey structure 
on an L-shaped plan-built c.1840 with projecting single-bay gable fronted entrance porch. It 
is in a poor state of repair however much of its historic fabric both externally and internally 
survives. 
Considering the above, the development of the former Matrons House is positive and 
welcome in bringing the structure back into use. The subdivision of the historic structure into 
2 no. separate units is deemed acceptable also. Subject to a number of minor design 
modifications, the works to the Matrons House is acceptable.
